brief: The battlefield is a floating 3D grid in cyberspace; the player is the “guardian process”, holding off malware that hides in normal traffic and heads for the “core”. The statement fixes the setting, three maps, six towers, six enemy types, three bosses and three items; art, models and colours are the model's design.

ul: Each of the three maps (14, 15 and 16 waves) has several switch nodes: with no other node isolated, isolating any one must send at least one entrance's enemies down a different road.

On reroute, enemies turn from where they are onto the new road, never teleporting or passing through blocked cells; new routes can be previewed before confirming, and nothing may leave an entrance or an enemy with no way through.
Towers have health and upgrade to level 2, with the honeypot and interceptor choosing one of two exclusive branches; resources are compute and intel, which cannot be exchanged.
The menu has three live demos under 60 seconds in all, with visible operations and back-and-forth fights; graphics, music and sound are all self-made.

points: **3D art**: finely modelled scenes, towers, enemies and bosses with distinct silhouettes, and continuous moving, attacking and hit reactions.
**Dynamic pathfinding**: isolation, destruction, bypass and boss terrain changes all recompute every path, and the way may never be sealed off.
**Mechanics carry the theme**: route length, fire coverage, tower survival and spending trade off, and each map calls for its own defence.
**Readable information**: with many enemies and effects on screen, routes, node states and health stay clear.
scoring: **Visuals are 65 points**: map and scene art 20, tower and enemy models and animation 20, effects and sound 12, interface and information 13.
**Gameplay is 35**: design thinking 10, combat 9 and the live demo 7 weigh most; pathfinding and rerouting itself is worth 3.
**Sound checked for implementation**: only whether ambience, music, event sounds and volume controls exist and are wired in, not how they sound.
**Scored on quality**: each point is scored within its value by how well it is done, and the odd small bug matters little.
